title: Reduction of the flat model
statement:
Let $A_{E,m}$ and $A_{E,n}$ be two finite coefficient stages with
$m\leq n$, let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, let
$K\in D^b_c(T,A_{E,n})$ be a bounded constructible complex of
$A_{E,n}$-modules on the small pro-étale site or on the small étale
site, and let $P\cong K$ be a bounded flat model of $K$ in degrees
$[a,b]$ in the sense of [lem-sf-flat-model]: each $P^q$ is a flat
$A_{E,n}$-module sheaf and $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Write
$K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ for the reduction of $K$. Then
$P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ is a bounded flat model of $K_m$ in the
same interval:

$$
K_m\cong P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m},\qquad
(P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m})^q=0\quad(q\notin[a,b]),
$$

and each term $P^q\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ is a flat
$A_{E,m}$-module sheaf. Consequently the reduction $K_m$ has finite
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ as soon
as $K$ does.

proof.text: On either site put $R=(A_{E,n})_T$ and $S=(A_{E,m})_T$. Since $\varpi_E^n=\varpi_E^m\varpi_E^{n-m}$, the identity of $\mathcal O_E$ induces $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ and hence $\varphi:R\to S$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use a skeleton and module values in the coefficient universe of [def-weil-size-convention]; the site is essentially small there. The complex $P$ is bounded above by $b$ with flat terms, so [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; blueprint proof, first sentence

proof.text: Let $Q_R,Q_S$ be the localizations. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the identity K-flat resolution of $P$ computes $L\varphi^*Q_R(P)$ as $Q_S(P\otimes_R S)$. Applying $L\varphi^*$ to the given $K\cong Q_R(P)$ gives $K_m\cong Q_S(P\otimes_R S)$ in $D(S)$, with its target $S$-module structure.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for the identity morphism of topoi with coefficient map R to S

proof.text: Set $P_m=P\otimes_R S$, with differentials $d_P^q\otimes1$. The K-flatness of step 1 and termwise flatness of $P$ meet both hypotheses of [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], so $P_m$ is K-flat over $S$ and each $P_m^q$ is flat over $S$. If $q\notin[a,b]$, then $P^q=0$; the sectionwise tensor presheaf $P^q(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)$ is zero, and so is its sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus $P_m$ is supported in $[a,b]$; with step 2 it is the asserted bounded flat model.

Assume the original Tor-amplitude hypothesis, so $a\le b$ on the pro-etale branch [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let $M$ be any $S$-module sheaf. The tensor tested there is that of [def-weil-derived-tensor] or [def-kun-derived-tensor]: for any K-flat model $P'$ of $K_m$ it is $Q_S(\operatorname{Tot}(P'\otimes_S M[0]))$, and since $M[0]$ has only degree zero, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] this total complex is $T_M(P')$, with differential $d_{P'}\otimes1+(-1)^q1\otimes0=d_{P'}\otimes1$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] to $P'$ and to $P_m$ (K-flat over $S$ by step 3): $Q_S(T_M(P'))\cong Q_S(P')\otimes_S^L M[0]\cong Q_S(P_m)\otimes_S^L M[0]\cong Q_S(T_M(P_m))$, the middle map induced by the isomorphisms of step 2. So whichever model the definition chooses, $K_m\otimes_S^L M$ is $Q_S(T_M(P_m))$, whose degree-$q$ term is $P_m^q\otimes_S M$. Outside $[a,b]$ this term is zero; its cohomology, a quotient of a kernel in that zero term [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], is zero. This is Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] or [def-kun-tor-amplitude].
